approved: Liability for Climate Change Damage (Make the Polluters Pay) Bill 2020
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would make fossil fuel companies legally responsible for damage caused by climate change.
It would allow victims, the Commonwealth Attorney-General, or a state or territory attorney-general to sue major emitters in the Federal Court for injunctions or damages.

A major emitter is defined as a company that produces fossil fuels or operates coal-fired power stations and emits over 1 million tonnes of greenhouse gases in any 12-month period starting on or after 1 September 1990.
Creates a new right for victims of climate change damage to sue fossil fuel companies.
Defines major emitters as those emitting over 1 million tonnes of greenhouse gases in a 12-month period since 1 September 1990.
Allows the court to assume a major emitter's share of damage is at least proportional to its share of global emissions.
Gives the Federal Court power to grant injunctions requiring emitters to reduce or cease activities causing future damage.
Applies the Act retrospectively from 1 July 2019.
Makes liability apply even if the production or operation was authorised by law.
Fossil fuel companies, including thermal coal, oil and gas producers and owners or operators of coal-fired power stations, and victims of climate change damage such as bushfire survivors.
